title: From boilers to balance sheets: LPG hike squeezes India’s textile hubs
content:
India’s textile and apparel hubs are reeling from a steep increase in commercial LPG prices, sharply inflating production costs amid weak global demand and intense price competition.
From Surat to Tiruppur and Noida, manufacturers face pressure from rising fuel and labour costs, while limited pricing power, worker shortages and infrastructure challenges are also squeezing margins and operations.

title: Liquidations continue to outpace resolutions under IBC: Ind-Ra
content:
India’s Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code recovery outcomes remain constrained by execution delays despite recent reforms, according to the Ind-Ra. 
In Q4 FY26, liquidation cases continued to outnumber resolutions, while recoveries stayed near 31 per cent of admitted claims. 
The agency said prolonged timelines, litigation delays, and NCLT capacity constraints continue to weigh on the insolvency process.

title: Bangladesh cabinet approves FDI Incentive Scheme policy
content:
The Bangladesh cabinet recently approved the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Incentive Scheme Policy, 2026.
The approval came at the cabinet’s ninth meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman. 
The policy aims at encouraging expatriate Bangladeshis and other Bangladeshi citizens to contribute to attracting FDI through the government’s incentive support.

title: India meets FY26 fiscal deficit target; ICRA flags FY27 risks
content:
India met its FY26 fiscal deficit target of 4.4 per cent of GDP, with the deficit contained at ₹15.2 trillion (~$159.7 billion) due to expenditure cuts and higher miscellaneous capital receipts, according to ICRA. 
However, the agency warned FY27 could see a 40-basis-point fiscal slippage amid West Asia conflict risks, rising subsidies and pressure on oil-related revenues and bond yields.

title: South India cotton yarn weakens as domestic, export demand slows
content:
India’s cotton yarn market stayed subdued this week as weak domestic and export demand weighed on prices in Mumbai and Tiruppur.
Spinning mills cut yarn rates due to sluggish buying and limited export inquiries.
Meanwhile, Gujarat cotton prices remained steady despite the duty exemption, supported by stable arrivals, cautious purchases, and unchanged CCI auction rates.

title: US Upland cotton sales rise 21%; Pima rebounds sharply: USDA
content:
US cotton export sales showed mixed trends in the week ended May 28.
Upland cotton net sales rose 21 per cent to 185,300 RB, led by Vietnam, Pakistan, Türkiye and China, though shipments fell 15 per cent.
Pima cotton sales rebounded 95 per cent to 5,400 RB, while exports reached a marketing-year high of 18,700 RB, driven by strong demand from India and Vietnam.

title: US’ Torrid Q1 FY26 sales fall 7.6% despite guidance beat
content:
Torrid Holdings reported first-quarter FY26 net sales of $245.8 million, down 7.6 per cent year-on-year, while net income fell to $0.4 million from $5.9 million. 
Comparable sales declined 1.7 per cent and adjusted EBITDA dropped to $17.6 million. 
The company closed 20 stores during the quarter and expects FY26 net sales between $940 million and $960 million.

title: Bangladesh garment exports slip to $35.3 bn in July-May
content:
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports fell 3.41 per cent year-on-year to $35.31 billion during July 2025-May 2026, with knitwear exports down 4.26 per cent and woven garments down 2.42 per cent.
Home textile exports rose 3.48 per cent to $853.26 million, while cotton product exports declined 11.23 per cent.
RMG and home textiles accounted for 82.57 per cent of the country’s total exports.
